regime_context: Detector shows a broad, two-tier precious-metals leadership (Gold Miners #1, Silver & Royalties #2, both eligible, durable, not crowded) with broad but non-committal rotation (56% breadth, low absorption, margin 0.173). The only validated leg is the absolute-trend gate (gate_helps true), so confidence is calibrated around trend-health/discipline rather than momentum rank. Given prev calls' low directional accuracy (0.372) despite 71% hit-rate, leans are intentionally humble.
emerging_watch: Watching whether the margin between Gold Miners and Silver & Royalties widens beyond 0.5 OR whether Base Metals & Copper (mean-revert tag, 0.51 durability) breaks out to overtake either precious-metals name on the eligible-trend measure — a confirmed handoff would retire the precious-metals-leadership read.

theses.subject: Gold Miners
theses.thesis: Gold Miners is the headline leader and ranks #1 with high breadth (0.933), decent durability (0.66), and the trend gate flags it eligible. The trend-following discipline (the one validated edge) argues for staying with the theme as long as it stays above its absolute-trend threshold — but momentum rank itself is a focus lens, not alpha.
theses.dissent: Precious metals leadership may be reflexively self-referential (attention spike) with no real return edge; r10 is slightly negative (-0.0054), suggesting momentum already cooled.

falsifier.text: XGD.TO trades below its own 20-day absolute-trend level (trend gate eligibility flips to false) before the check-by date

theses.subject: Silver & Royalties
theses.thesis: Silver & Royalties is the confirmed challenger to Gold Miners (margin only 0.173) with similar breadth (0.917) and durability (0.63), also eligible and not crowded. It is a companion precious-metals lean in the same trend cohort.
theses.dissent: Both gold and silver share the same ETF proxy (XGD.TO), so this is not a genuinely independent theme — it adds concentration to the same precious-metals beta rather than diversification.

falsifier.text: XGD.TO lags XBM.TO (base metals) by more than 5% over a rolling 10-day window before the check-by date

theses.subject: Base Metals & Copper
theses.thesis: Base Metals & Copper is rank 3, eligible, but with lower durability (0.51) and a mean-revert hurst tag — suggesting the trend is less persistent than gold. The trend gate still passes, so a modest tilt is defensible under discipline, but this is the weakest of the eligible materials cohort.
theses.dissent: Mean-revert tag plus lower breadth (0.667) signals the trend may already be stalling; copper is closely tied to global industrial demand which the prevailing macro backdrop (AI tech, geopolitics) does not clearly support.

falsifier.text: XBM.TO's 20-day average flips below its 50-day average before the check-by date

macro_narrative.note: market-level macro/policy/geo narrative flow; coincident, not per-theme, never a trigger
